Next: Danielle to send Converge HCI vs vSphere renewal comparison. Get intro to Marcus Russo.

author: Danielle Pelletier
subject: vSphere 6.7 / Converge HCI comparison
body:
Hi Cameron,

As promised on the call with Priya, attached is a side-by-side for the control center cluster:

- Option A: renew VMware under the new per-core subscription on existing hosts (your 10 Atlas 140s) - 3yr subscription only, no hardware.
- Option B: 4-node Converge HCI with built-in hypervisor, migrate the historian/GIS/OMS VMs, reuse 4 of the Atlas 140s as a Vault proxy + test cluster.

B is higher year-1, lower over 3 years based on the core counts you sent. Happy to walk through it. Also - your Strata 500 (5TXHLSN) is at ~67% per telemetry and growing ~3.7TB/mo, worth including in the plan.

Thanks,
Danielle Pelletier
Inside Infrastructure Specialist | Orvane Technologies

Something's happening. CRM still says Retention but no buys since Mar 2024.

author: Priya Brennan
subject: AI pilot discovery - Marcus Russo
body:
Finally got Marcus Russo (VP Eng). He owns the AI pilot, IT (Cameron/Quinn) supports.

Pilot (since ~May):
1. Computer vision on drone + helicopter inspection imagery of transmission lines - detect damaged insulators, vegetation encroachment. ~1.1PB of imagery archived in cloud object storage, ~40TB/mo new during inspection season.
2. LLM over 15 years of maintenance work orders + outage reports for crews ("what failed last time on this feeder").

Running on public cloud GPU instances. Cloud bill for the pilot ~$40-45K/month and climbing. Marcus wants to go to production by summer storm season; his estimate is 3x the pilot compute.

Concerns pushing them on-prem: egress costs on the imagery, CIP compliance reviewers uncomfortable with grid asset data in public cloud, GPU instance availability (got capacity errors twice).

Competition: Lumora has already pitched GPU servers to Cameron. Cloud provider offering a committed-use discount.

Next: get Danielle/infra on a sizing call. New CFO is Owen Medina (joined in Aug - James Parker left in July, explains the bounce).

author: Tamara Reynolds
subject: Atlas AI technical discovery
body:
Attendees: Marcus Russo (VP Eng), Cameron Cox (Dir IT), Mitchell Ward (Dir Network Eng), Vikram Friedman (Infra Mgr), Quinn Reynolds (Dir IT); Tamara Reynolds (Infra specialist, started 11/22), Priya Brennan, Devin Campbell

Workloads:
- CV training on inspection imagery: retrain monthly, ~6 days per run on 32 cloud GPUs today. Model + batch needs >=80GB GPU memory.
- LLM: fine-tuned mid-size open model (~70B) for work-order Q&A, ~300 internal users, latency target <3s.

Facilities / power:
- Control center DC racks are 5kW feeds. Atlas AI 8-GPU node ~10kW peak each. Need 2 racks re-fed (2x 30A 3-phase each) + rear-door cooling or put in backup DC which has 12kW racks.
- Generator capacity OK per facilities. Cameron leaning backup DC too.

Network: Mitchell wants a separate 100GbE fabric, not on the core. He used Mesh at his last company (Lake Valley Engineering) - positive. VLANs for GPU mgmt/BMC on OOB network.

Storage: Strata 500 (5TXHLSN) 78% full, +3.7TB/mo; Strata 300 (T6GMFCN) 82%; Strata Scale node (2655B9M) 79%. None has an NVMe tier. Vault DP8900 G6C3QR5 at ~92% - separate problem, flagged. Imagery would stay in cloud object storage cold, hot set (~250TB) on-prem.

Hypervisor: AI nodes bare metal + Kubernetes, NOT on vSphere 6.7.

Security: 27 advisories still open on existing gear (146 remediated, 3 risk accepted) - Cameron wants new BMCs on the OOB network from day one.

Competitive: Lumora quoted 2 GPU servers last month - Marcus says cheaper but no storage/network story.

Actions:
- Tamara: sizing + power draft by 12/17.
- Devin: ProCare + deployment + data center services scope.
- Priya: TCO model vs cloud for Owen Medina. Offer Atlas AI POC/loaner.

author: Priya Brennan
subject: AI infrastructure - what I need to see
body:
Priya,

Marcus brought me up to speed. Before this goes anywhere near the board I need:

1. 3-year TCO: on-prem vs. staying in cloud with the committed-use discount we've been offered. Include power, cooling, the rack work, staff time. Don't hide the facilities cost.
2. Financing options - we're in a cost reduction program, a $640K capex line won't fly as-is. Does Orvane Financial Services do consumption/Flex on this kind of gear?
3. What happens to the hardware if the pilot doesn't go to production.

I'd like this by Jan 16.

Owen Medina
CFO, Peterson & Kennedy Utilities Group
